title: The Easiest Loaf of Bread
description: With just five everyday ingredients, simple instructions, and no advanced techniques, this European-style crusty bread is an ideal starting point for anyone learning how to make bread. It truly is “the easiest loaf of bread you’ll ever bake” — thanks in large part to King Arthur Unbleached Bread Flour, whose high protein content ensures excellent structure, a lofty rise, and satisfying texture. If you're still learning how to make bread, be sure to watch Martin demonstrate the key techniques of this recipe in our video, The Easiest Loaf of Bread You'll Ever Bake.

ingredients.raw_text: 4 1/2 to 5 cups (540g to 600g) King Arthur Unbleached Bread Flour
yellow cornmeal, for coating the pan

steps.body: Weigh your flour, or measure it by gently spooning it into a cup, then sweeping off any excess.

Stir together all of the ingredients except the cornmeal, starting with 4 1/2 cups (540g) of the flour, using a sturdy spoon or a stand mixer fitted with the beater paddle, until everything comes together in a rough, shaggy mass of dough.

To knead by hand, turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface, using some of the additional 1/2 cup (60g) of flour as needed. Fold the far edge back toward you, press it away with the heels of your hands, and rotate the dough 90°. Repeat this fold-press-rotate motion with a rocking motion until the dough is bouncy and smooth.

To knead in a stand mixer, switch to the dough hook and knead at medium speed until the dough is smooth, elastic, and a bit bouncy. If it does not form a ball that clears the sides of the bowl, sprinkle in just enough of the additional flour to make this happen.

Place the dough in a bowl lightly greased with vegetable oil or cooking spray, cover airtight, and let it rise at room temperature until doubled in size, about 1 to 2 hours. If your kitchen is below 65°F, rise the dough in the turned-off oven with the light on.
Gently deflate the dough, cut it in half, and pat each half into a rough 6" x 8" oval.

Fold each piece like a business letter: fold one short side into the center, fold the other short side over it, and press the open edge closed with the heel of your hand. Gently pat and roll the dough into a log about 10" long.
Place the loaves seam-side down on a baking sheet (lined with parchment if desired), and sprinkle the pan or parchment generously with cornmeal.
Let the loaves rise, lightly covered with greased plastic wrap, until puffy. They are ready when a gently poked finger indentation remains.
Toward the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
While the oven preheats, place an empty cast-iron frying pan on the lowest rack.
Bring 1 cup of water to a boil in the microwave or on the stovetop.
When the bread is risen, use a sieve to dust the loaves with a thin coat of flour, then make three or four 1/2" deep diagonal slashes in each loaf.
Place the bread in the oven, pour the boiling water into the frying pan below, and quickly shut the oven door. Wear good oven mitts to shield your hands and arms from the steam.
Bake the bread for 20 to 25 minutes, until the crust is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. The interior should register at least 190°F on a digital thermometer.
Turn the oven off, crack the door open, and leave the bread inside for 5 additional minutes to help keep the crust crisp.
Remove the bread from the oven and cool it on a rack. Avoid cutting into it until it has cooled a bit, since cutting hot bread can negatively affect its texture.
Store the bread, well-wrapped, at room temperature for a couple of days. Freeze for longer storage.
